title: Notes of Ministry - 3 - February 1973

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 3 - February 19 (2027)/Notes of Ministry - 3 - Februar - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: I thought the Lord would further help us, beloved brethren, in seeing that the great truth of the prophet, the priest, and the king does not cease whatever the days of difficulty may be.

Haggai and Zechariah, as we know, are two post-captivity prophets; they came in after the captivity. These two men prophesied to a remnant of the people, that is, to Judah. Not only did they prophesy, but they helped the people, indicating that it is not just a question of saying something, or of conveying a message, even if the message be from God, but it says of them “and with them were the prophets of God, who helped them”. So that we are to be helpers one of another.

It is interesting to see how the prophet, and the priest, and the king are carried through. It is true Zerubbabel is not called the king; he is called the governor. Nevertheless, it is evident that the great principle of rule is there, so that, whatever the conditions that may exist among God’s people, whatever the breakdown, or abuse of such expressions as “the governor”, it does not alter the fact that the principle of rule among God’s people is essential.

The first characteristic that I would like to bring before you in days such as those in which Haggai lived, is that of the prophet. It is at the mouth of the prophet that the people lived. I believe that it is at the mouth of the prophet at the moment that we are guided through the wilderness; that is, by continuous speaking from God, whatever the conditions that may exist.
If you think of the time when Haggai prophesied, you might have said everything had gone.

There had been a movement in revival and a certain upbuilding of what was according to God and pleasing to Him, but through the efforts of certain opposers it had stopped. We might say the whole position had gone to ruin again. What a sad thing, dear brethren, that what began in the early 1800’s has come to a public shame; there is no question about that. God has allowed it to be so, so that books are written which show a complete exposure publicly of what is called the movement of the brethren. How humbling that is! Yet for all that, God, in mercy, has not ceased speaking to His people.
Now Haggai comes in at a juncture in the history of the recovery when there was a re-stirring.

I believe God would help us in spite of the fact that we have had a breakdown; we might say another breakdown, and we could add yet another breakdown; God would help us to listen to His word and give us to understand that in His mercy He has not ceased speaking to us. As we said in the reading, we could raise this question with any believer who might choose to come into such a meeting; Are you prepared to listen to the present word of God? Are you exercised to be in touch with the prophetic speaking? Some say, It is finished. Others have shut themselves away in their homes saying, “No collective position; nothing of the character of the assembly; nothing substantial that represents it; everything has gone, and there is no divine speaking”.

We tend to think that God would act as we would act in such circumstances. “That is how they treated me, and I will treat them the same”. That is not God. God’s mercy is ever evident to His beloved people in whatever conditions they may find themselves. I think God’s speaking is always appropriate to the moment and never intended just to give us information.

If we take the long view that was referred to in the reading—if we look right forward to the city of which it says, “I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of the heaven from God, having the glory of God”—that is not just for information; it is intended to have its own moral effect that there might be a reflection today of the character of what is seen in that city.

So it is with the prophet. Isaiah can prophesy; he speaks of the day yet to come when the wolf shall lie down with the lamb, when the child shall be unafraid and the boys and girls shall play in the streets of Jerusalem. The prophet can look forward and see those conditions when Jesus is supreme. It is intended, however, to have an immediate effect upon the people.

So the prophecy is for the people to whom it is directed. May I say again, not to give them information merely, but to give an understanding that God will reach His purpose and to strengthen their hand in the present testimony. That is what God will do for us, I think, as He indicates to us that His purpose is sure, and that everything is settled in the Man Who has gone into His presence. Christ Jesus—we might say the ark gone in and everything established for the pleasure of God. It is not intended simply to tell us that it is so, but to have its own effect upon us that we might have grace and power to continue in His testimony.

So Paul says, “Be not therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me His prisoner”. Some might say, ‘What is the testimony of our Lord?’ I expect you know J.N.D.’s answer to that, and J.T.’s too, I believe; it is the glad tidings. Think of how comprehensive that is! Think of what it is to God to have a company of persons devoted to our Lord, who are cherishing in their souls in the very presence of opposing forces the secret of the fact that God has another Man in another world and presently He is going to display it. God has here in testimony at the moment, and I believe will have until the end, that which He will display in the world to come. Well, that is very encouraging.

Now this prophet comes in with a word from God. The people are not left to themselves, because “where there is no vision the people cast off restraint”. That is what will happen to us, dear brethren, if we have no vision, where there is no prophetic word. We referred to Samuel lying down in the temple. J.T. said, “Who taught him to lie down in the temple?”

Was it the proper place to lie down? Was it ever said in the law that persons should lie down in the temple? You may say that it was his proper place; it is called his place. But in the temple, as far as I see, the priests stand to minister to Jehovah. The temple is no place to lie down. Who taught him that? It was probably Eli, the priest who could not see! Solemn thing!
Of course, God took up Samuel and gave him a word, so that through that man there was a vision in a dark day, and so, too, Haggai the prophet had a word for the people in a dark day.

You may say, “This is no time to build the house of God”. I believe it is time we energetically set ourselves to build. How do we do that? I say, we build the truth into one another. How do we speak? What do we say? What is the subject of our conversation? Let us not wait until the enemy attacks and then begin to emphasise principles. Let us be ever seeking to build the truth into the souls of one another so that, when the enemy attacks, there are persons governed by the principles they have been taught; which they have learned to love, and in which they have been built up. That, I think, is what is essential.

So God says, You looked for much and it was but little. In His own ways in government these things had come upon them. Did they just happen? We think back even in our own short history. Have the crises that have come upon us just happened? Or has God been in them? I would say that God has been in them. I have often thought of Rehoboam. Think of that man’s utter stupidity! Instead of listening to the older men who stood with Solomon, he listened to the younger men and caused a division in Israel. The height of folly; and yet the word says it was brought about by God. God caused it to bring to pass His word through the prophet to Jeroboam (2 Chronicles 10: 15). Some people say, What stupidity there has been in our day!

There is no doubt about that. In fact, I am sure that things done recently were also stupid. But God caused them to bring to pass His word. God is in these matters and we need to understand it, and He is in these matters to sift and search His people to bring out reality and to bring out those who are prepared to go on in the path of discipleship and not merely be the recipients of blessing.
“Jehovah stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah”. I wonder if we are prepared to recognise the principle of authority in our localities. You say,

‘Well, there is only one brother in our locality so it does not apply’. You are quite sure of that? J.T. said the first principle of government is self-government. Whether it is one brother, two brothers, one brother one sister, two brothers two sisters, the principle of authority in God’s assembly still applies. He stirred up the spirit of the governor, and we do need, I believe, to recognise this great principle of rule among the people of God. It was introduced with Israel; it will be introduced among the nations, and it is imperative that we understand Christ’s authority in the assembly. J.T. brought that before us, and through him God caused light to shine on the need of Christ’s authority in the assembly; not only the recognition of absolute authority in Himself, but delegated authority, and an authority that operates in the assembly for the protection of what is precious to God in these dark days.

Now it says also, “And Jehovah stirred up ... the spirit of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people”, so that you have the prophet introducing the mind of God; you have the governor representing the authority of God among His people, and then you have the high priest. We would fully understand, dear brethren, that these things are seen in their perfection in Jesus, the great King, “the city of the great King”, and “having a great Priest over the house of God”, and again it is said of Him “the great Shepherd of the sheep”—everything perfectly seen in that Man. His assembly reflects Himself, and I believe these great characteristics are to be seen working out among us, yielding honour and glory to Himself. Now this applies in the darkest day. It applies when there has been a breakdown, and it applies when there has been another breakdown Then it says, “Jehovah stirred up ... the spirit of all the remnant of the people”. As far as the assembly is concerned, I think we understand there is no teaching of the remnant, because the Lord always has the whole thing before Him. So when He speaks to the assembly. He says, “To the angel of the assembly in Philadelphia”, or “To the angel of the assembly in Laodicea”. Let me remind you of this, beloved brethren, that the fact that the church has broken down publicly has not changed its responsibility at all. Sometimes we think it has.

The church is a responsible body to Christ. That is a sobering reflection. But, you say, has not the breakdown itself dissolved it? Has it not negated it? Never! The responsibility of the church as set here to be a witness to Christ remains. He presents Himself to Laodicea as “the faithful and true witness”.
Why does He say that? Because the church had failed to be the witness, and it was maintained in Himself; but the church as a body is still responsible to Himself and we need to understand that.

Nevertheless, although we cannot speak of the remnant of the church, the spirit of that applies in a dark day. I would like to ask God to stir up our spirits. I suppose we would have to regard ourselves as the spirit of the remnant of the people. I doubt if anybody here would dare to call himself the governor! I expect you would be accused of being in the “system” if you did! And I doubt if anybody would dare to call himself the great high priest, or anything like that. We can, however, put ourselves in the spirit of the remnant of the people. Oh, beloved brethren, let us be with God as priests that He will stir up the spirits of His people! Now that does not just apply to those with whom we walk. Do you not think we could ask God to revive His work in the midst of the days in others? You notice the word about one of the kings was that many fell away to him when they saw that Jehovah was with him (2
Chronicles 15: 9), and if there is a practical evidence that the Lord is with us, I believe many would fall away to where the Lord is in the testimony.

Let us receive the prophetic word and let us be with God as priests, calling upon Him as another prophet did, to revive His work in the midst of the days, accepting shame, taking responsibility—not claiming to be something to which we expect God to add, but taking lowly ground, desiring that through His work others might come into the light of the truth and the maintenance of what is proper to the assembly, and the keeping of the principles which govern the fellowship of His Son.

All this is involved in the building, and he says, “Go up to the mountain”, and that means exercise. If it is a question of teaching and building, you go up the mountain; if it is a question of feeding, you are quiet and restful, and sit down on the green grass. So you get both; sometimes you sit down and feed as the flock does, at other times you go up the mountain to be taught, as the disciples went up the mountain to Jesus, and “having opened His mouth, He taught them”. On another occasion He said, “Sit down on the green grass”. So we need both. In Haggai Jehovah says, “Go up to the mountain and bring wood”. Be exercised to bring in, and build among the saints, the order of man that is pleasing to God, even Jesus Christ, the Foundation and Corner Stone, which shows that there is no deterioration throughout the whole of the building.

I think we could rightly be with God that He would stir up the spirit of the remnant of the people, and that would include us, and at the same time give us to be exercised about a prophetic word. If God does not guide us we certainly cannot guide ourselves. “He shall guide you into all the truth”, and we should listen to the prophetic word as it reaches us week by week—some say, month by month, but shall we say week by week? If we do not listen, we shall lose our way. We must listen to what God is saying, because He is the Guide.

“In the desert God will teach thee
What the God that thou hast found
Patient, gracious, powerful, holy;
All His grace shall there abound.”

It is divine light through the prophetic word that guides the saints through the wilderness and we need to give way increasingly to what God says to us week by week—and day by day, I suppose we could say too—and be maintained as we listen to the living word that reaches us; penetrating, but having its own effect to keep us in touch with God and in the path of His will.

You will notice in chapter 2 that this prophet spoke, then spoke again, and then he spoke yet again. He does not say, “Well, I spoke this week so it is someone else’s turn next week”. He does not take that line at all; he is a prophet.

So it was said to John, “Thou shalt prophesy again”. The prophet is the prophet, and the prophet should always be prepared to deliver his message, as it says, “the message of Jehovah through the messenger of Jehovah”, and we need to be prepared to recognise the messengers of Jehovah.

If a brother stands up with a faulty expression and not, in our opinion, having very much ability, what message is the Lord endeavouring to convey to us? The priests, or the spiritual, will discern it, dear brethren, and not be hindered by the vessel, or by the character of the messenger.

Jehovah’s messenger is anxious to get what the Lord would convey to His people. I would urge it upon us that we should be exercised to get the message the Lord is seeking to convey to His people to keep them alive in the desert in these days.

Now in Ezra 5 I wanted particularly to call attention to the fact that it says that they helped the people. “Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews that were in Judah and Jerusalem; in the name of the God of Israel did they prophesy to them. Then rose up Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and began to build the house of God which is at Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, who helped them”. In other words, the prophets did not do all the speaking and the other persons all the work, but the prophets were prepared to do the work, they

“helped them”. You think of one being called a helper of Paul. Think of Paul saying “these hands”—he is lowly enough to gather a bundle of sticks in days when there had been confusion, breakdown and shipwreck. I think we would have to admit that we have been in a shipwreck, but can we be in a lowly spirit gathering sticks? The enemy will attack and come out of the very heat that is provided by the gathering, but he is thrown off, and I believe, dear brethren, as we are committed to the Lord, as we listen to His word, as we are helpers one of another and building the truth into one another, so the efforts of the enemy against Christ and the assembly will be negated.

May we be found in this spirit and may we, if we have taken away nothing else from these meetings, be impressed with the need amongst us of the prophet, and the priest, and the king, for His Name’s sake.

No doubt the passage in Luke 9 points to the kingdom. The day will yet come when Jesus will be supreme in glory, and the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of God as the waters cover the sea—a wonderful day to look forward to! Perhaps we have little conception of what it will be, but I believe the Spirit of God would give us an impression of it so that we may have amongst the brethren now some knowledge of the heavenly influence of Jesus. It is a heavenly influence. He was on earth, but He was never earthly. He was a heavenly Man on earth. That reminds me of the words of J.N.D. about the assembly “an unearthly witness of heavenly things on earth”. So we are to be characteristically like Him, dear brethren.

Of course, we must first of all accept that we are not naturally like Him. None of us is heavenly. We are earthly. We may not be worldly, and you may argue that you are not worldly, and do not go in for the things of the world. You don’t go in for their pleasures, their pursuits, nor are you ambitious, involved in politics, sport, or such things. Often where I find I am tested is that I am earthly. You may live in your garden. I always remember Mr. Biggs telling us an incident in the life of a brother who got astray. He lost his way and went out of fellowship, and he became a keen gardener. He lived in a village where there was a half-wit, and one day the half-wit passed by, looked over the fence, and said to the brother, “Oh, Mr. —, you live in your garden, don’t you?” The Lord used that to go right home to his conscience, and he was restored.

Where do you live? Where do I live? I am not implying at all that if you have a garden you should not dig it, and produce from it. But the question is, “Where do you live?” Jesus was a very simple when He was here; simple in His life—and I believe, as a lowly Man, very simple in His ways. So He said, “Consider the lilies”. If He says consider them, you do it.

Have you ever considered the lilies? He also said, look at the birds. Have you ever looked at the birds? You say, “All that has moral meaning”. Yes, true; but the Lord said, look at the birds. As you look at the birds you can take account of their habits. I don’t mean you become a specialist, a bird watcher, or something like that, as a profession or hobby, but He said, look at the birds. So Jesus was here a lowly, heavenly Man—coming down here in all the grace of heaven to take up the simplicity of things in life.
He gave His Father delight; and as that character in any way marks us, we give the Father delight. We should love, dear brethren, to practise the things that are pleasing in His sight.

Well, here, Jesus goes up into the mountain. He did not go up to be transfigured; it says He went up to pray. That was the reason. And as He prayed the fashion of His countenance became different. And I believe in this gospel He is a Pattern, especially the Pattern for us.

How often we are challenged as to how far we pray deliberately. I find it is necessary, and a great privilege, to be deliberate in prayer. And I think you will find as you pray that often it is necessary to persevere, and in the power of the Spirit of God you are drawn into a greater appreciation of the Person in Whose presence you are. It is possible, I believe, for praying persons to become different. I am not suggesting, of course, that there was anything about Jesus that needed to be removed, or judged, as there is with us. What I am suggesting is that, as a perfect Pattern for us, He would encourage us to pray. We might have thought, surely the point in this is the glory of the transfiguration; but it says, “He went up to pray”. And in this gospel in particular, as we all very well know, He is particularly pointed out as the praying Man.

In conversing with one or two brothers recently I have found that they have had kindred exercises with mine—the Lord has brought them to a point experimentally where they have felt their utter dependence upon Him. Everything seems shut up. Sometimes you feel you hardly reach God in your prayer. When I say reach Him I mean to be conscious that He is listening to you. You may say, “But I understand that God listens to everything, the faintest, feeblest cry will reach Him”. Yes, you know that objectively, but as we pray, beloved brethren, I believe it delights the Lord when we reach the consciousness that He is listening to us. Jesus said, you remember, “I know that Thou hearest Me always”. That word ‘know’ is conscious knowledge. Think of that Man in His perfection, whatever the circumstances, congenial or otherwise, mainly otherwise. He was conscious that His Father always heard Him. I could not say that.

Do you find, as others sometimes feel, and I must confess to such a feeling, that the heavens do sometimes seem like brass’? And the earth sometimes seems like iron, and you seem to get nowhere and give up in despair. Have you ever done that? What I find is the need for perseverance. You may say, “I kneel down; I’m so tired, I fall asleep”. And what do you do when you wake up? Are you so disgusted with yourself that you get into bed? No—persevere! Go on praying. Wake up, and pray again! These are practical, simple matters which most of us would have to admit that at some time or another we have experienced. I believe that when it says that He went up into the mountain to pray, it is intended to show the deliberate attitude that Jesus took to prayer. Not constant, simple speaking in His daily life—which was true and good—and true and good for us, but a deliberate attitude of mind; He went up there, and “as He prayed, the fashion of His countenance became different”; a praying Man, a dependent Man, going into the glory.

You may say, “Is that possible for us?” I would like to ask you if you are committed to it. We all feel our weakness, as our brother expressed in the reading. None of us would excuse ourselves, or elect ourselves out of what he said as to weakness and feeling our limitation; how little we are in touch with the Lord in the present testimony in its power. But I believe it gives the Lord some delight when we are committed to it. Are you committed to it? What will it mean if I am committed to it? Take the younger men. I would counsel you in your youth to go in for the truth. Go in for reading the scriptures; go in for prayer; be deliberate. Satan would turn you aside, and you will always find something that you must just do before you pray. You must do this, or that. But be deliberate. When you go into your chamber, the Lord says, “Shut thy door”. You say, “Of course, that doesn’t mean literally”. Are you sure it doesn’t mean literally? That is what He says, “Shut thy door”. It is deliberate. And “pray to thy Father Who is in secret, and thy Father Who sees in secret will render it to thee”. You may say, “You are saying a lot about prayer”. Beloved brethren, I believe it is the secret of access into everything. It is simple and implicit dependence on God. A praying man recognises two things, at any rate. One is, that he has a need, and he has no strength in himself; the other is that He is speaking to someone Who is willing to meet that need, that is, our glorious Resource, the Father.

Now here Jesus goes up to pray, and the fashion of His countenance became different. We find here a picture of His heavenly kingdom and glory, but to be held in testimony. Of course, it is bound up among the disciples; but it is held in testimony. And I believe that the Lord would strengthen us by some impression in the present moment in testimony that the glory is about to be revealed. So we are looking forward. It says, “We boast in hope of the glory of God”—boast in hope of it. That is not the glory we are going into there; it is the glory that is coming out, that will yet burst upon this poor benighted scene. Have you the secret of that in your soul? If you have the secret of it, and the secret of Jesus as the Centre of it, I believe it will strengthen you not only in submission to Himself, but in the testimony and enable you to shine in His spirit. So these two men speak of His departure. It does not say they spoke of His death, although, of course, that was the means of it; but they spoke of His departure, that is, out of one scene into another of which He was to be, and was, the Sun and the Centre. How wonderful to think of that I believe that prayer, dependence upon God, is the avenue out of one scene into another. He has, of course, gone before; but I believe it takes us in the spirit of the mind, from the scene of need into the scene where there is no need. Would you not like to touch that? I think the Lord would help us to touch it. But, we need to persevere in prayer.

You never tell people to persevere in things that are easy, do you? You tell them to persevere in things which are difficult. So persevere in prayer. Keep on keeping on, if you like. As the prophet said, “Give Him no rest”.

Now in the next section we find two persons who are enthusiastic. Perhaps we have been that way. They are thinking about the Lord, and I do not doubt that they loved Him. And maybe they had been thinking about those two men, Moses and Elias. Perhaps they had thought about their history, as we would. We go back and think about Moses, the meekest man in all the earth. Then we think of Elijah, of the man who says, “If I be a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume thee and thy fifty” (2 Kings 1: 12). That is what they must have been thinking about. Elijah also was on the mountain. “Wilt Thou that we speak that fire come down from heaven and consume them, as also Elias did?” Think of such a spirit as that; but they did not know the spirit they were of. It is so with us, dear brethren. It is unwitting; often it is ignorance—it is put down as a sin of ignorance. We think we are so enthusiastic for the truth, and press the truth. In a certain sense that is right. You will quote J.B.S. against me. He said, “Press the truth and it will show where the error is”. But to force it, is not of God, and so often in our enthusiasm we overlook the fact that we are not of the right spirit.

Jesus therefore rebuked them. He says, “Ye know not of what spirit ye are”. I wonder whether we do? This is written for us. It is written for you and me, and we are reading today, in November 1972, what is intended for our benefit. Of what spirit am I? It is not, What do I say? but, Of what spirit am I? Jesus says, “Ye know not”. These Samaritans rejected Him. It may be said, “These persons have turned away their minds from the truth”. And what is your spirit going to be? I think we need to watch our spirit, and watch what we say, and the way we speak about the brethren from whom we have had to part company. We must maintain the truth, and it is very clear that there can be no fellowship with them. It is equally true that there should be no bitterness against them. Bitterness is not right; it is not of God; it comes from the flesh. No fellowship does not mean that there is bitterness. You may be accused of it, but just watch your spirit as regards these dear brethren. You must go on in the truth.

Pursue the truth; maintain the truth—and fraternising in this eating and drinking and sitting down to play with those not in the fellowship, or the power of the fellowship of God’s Son, is against the truth. That does not mean that you are bitter; you would love to see every one of them restored on the ground of the truth, and you feel it that there can be no fellowship.
Nevertheless the Lord says to them, “Ye know not of what spirit ye are”.

Then they went to another village. That is sobering. The fact is this, that while fire is not to be called down from heaven upon the village that refused Him, they would have to face the fact that they missed Him. That would be in God’s ways, in God’s government. That means they do not get the gain of His presence. The persons who refuse Jesus, and who refuse the truth, and who refuse to see what He is doing and relate themselves to it, will miss His presence. As far as we are concerned, however, there is to be no bitterness or calling down of fire, or the spirit of it. But at the same time, in God’s ways they miss the presence of Jesus. That is sobering. What will we do? Where are we? The Lord would raise the challenge with us in these days as to what the banner in the power of the Spirit is. There is our desire to hold to the truth in the spirit of Christ, but this is not a free-and-easy attitude toward everybody and everything. The spirit of Christ is a firm, simple, and unflinching pursuit of the path of the will of God in the spirit of meekness; not holding to one’s own rights, but to the rights of God.

Now there is a very natural kind of question that arises when we speak like this. You say, We sit together; we love one another, and it is very easy to speak about these things when we are sitting together. But the pertinent question that arises is, “How can I come out in the spirit of Christ, I who am so unlike Him? I find that immediately something is done against me I retaliate.” You find that, I do not doubt, because you come from the same stock as I do. And therefore if I say what I find in my heart naturally, then I am sure you find it in yours. That again reminds me of the word of J.N.D., “No thought or motive that ever existed in the heart of Jesus ever exists in mine naturally, and no thought or motive that exists in my heart naturally ever existed in His”. So completely different is the kind of man. But how am I to reach His spirit? Has everybody here in this company received the Holy Spirit from a glorified Man? That is a very searching question for us. We should not take it for granted.

Maybe we should ask our younger brethren if they have had a personal transaction with a glorified Man. I never tire of repeating an incident in my own life when I heard Edward McBride give an address and very searchingly say, “How far is a glorified Man in heaven a reality to your soul?” I have never forgotten it. How far is He a reality to you? Have you received the Spirit from Him?

Now in chapter 10 we have someone who sat down at the feet of Jesus and was listening to His word. That is deliberate. It was not that she was about her business and was—thinking that is very good, of course. But she sat down and was listening. I think, brethren, we need deliberately to make time for prayer, and make time for sitting down. “Of course it is not literal”, you say. But why not literal? It says, “She sat down”, and I think there is something in that, you know, to know what it is. A brother pointed out to me that in the passage we read earlier in 2 Timothy 4, it says, “The Lord stood with me”. In another place it says He sat Himself down on the right hand of the greatness on high; but He stood with a man who was standing in the truth. Now of this dear sister it says she sat down. We all find there is not much time for that; there is so much to do; life is so busy, with meetings, much to do in the house, entertaining, and so on. And we would say, “After all, someone has to do it!” I know a young sister who is very often reminding me that someone has to do the washing up—which is perfectly true. She expresses—and other sisters have expressed—a certain sympathy with Martha, because someone must do the work. Notwithstanding, Mary found time to sit down at the feet of Jesus and listen to His word. It was not that she just heard it. She listened—are you listening? You say, “Well, I am only listening to someone saying a word of encouragement”. When we listen to an address we should listen for the Lord’s voice. Do you listen to hear what He is saying? It may be that the person speaking is frail. Maybe he has not much to say, but you listen that in the words that he expresses the Lord will convey something to your soul. That is what is needed. You may find that much is said today you will forget, but there is something the Lord would communicate to every listening person. I would like to be in that state. These two sisters suggest two states of soul. One is a state of soul that is rather agitated; the other is a state of soul that is restful and listening to His word.
One of the old-time worthies said that Mary listened to the whole counsel of God from the lips of that Man. What a thing that is! Well, do we do that?

We now come back to prayer. It says in chapter 11, “As He was in a certain place praying, when He ceased, one of His disciples said to Him, Lord, teach us to pray, even as John also taught his disciples”. Of course you don’t need to be taught to pray, do you? Do you think you need to be taught to pray? Surely you just kneel down and say what you want, and that is it. “Lord, teach us to pray”; do you mean to tell me the brethren need to be taught to pray? Well, that is what someone said and I can understand him saying it after he heard Jesus pray. “Father, as to those whom Thou hast given Me, I desire that where I am they also may be with Me” (John 17: 24)—think of the spirit of the great Priest looking right down the dispensation. As you hear, and get into the spirit of that prayer, you say to the Lord, almost unconsciously, “Lord, teach us to pray”. Not all my wants and woes, but what is the burden of that prayer of the great Priest? It is for the testimony and the will and the interests of His God and Father. So you can understand their saying as they listened to Jesus, “Teach us to pray”; because “we do not know what we should pray for as is fitting, but the Spirit joins its help to our weakness”, so that we might know how to pray according to the will of God. May we be helped in that feature, dear brethren.

The next thing that I draw attention to is the receiving of Holy Spirit. “How much rather shall the Father who is in heaven give (the) Holy Spirit to them that ask Him?” Will you say, “Of course I do not do that: I do not ask for Him because I have received Him years ago. My sins were forgiven and I received the Holy Spirit 40 years ago!” and that is that. But, you know, from the point of view of this scripture, that is not that at all! This is characteristic. I may receive the Spirit and grieve Him. I may have received the Spirit and quench Him, quench the fire or the flow. Do you ask the Father every day for Holy Spirit?—not exactly that you should receive Him as you received Him initially, but that you might receive Him in the sense of His character marking every word and every action at every moment. How testing I find that is, even as I say it. But I believe it is in the Lord’s mind that we should ask for Holy Spirit. It is true that once you have received Him. He never departs from you; you are sealed for the day of redemption (Ephesians 4: 30). But I believe it is essential day by day, if we are to reach something of the Spirit, and right submission to the Lord Jesus, that we should daily be seeking the Father’s face, and seeking His help, that we might receive the Spirit in a characteristic way, so as to proceed here in the testimony of God.

May the Lord help us, dear brethren, through our simple time together, as to the spirit and kingdom of our Lord, that we might be here more for Him, more subject to Him; more shining in His spirit, and more committed to the testimony; and that as we are more committed to His testimony we might each of us know what it is to be in the secret and power of the present testimony, though there are but few in it, and I think that has always been the case.
If I may repeat what I said in London—F.E.R. said it at any time in the history of the testimony you could number on the fingers of one hand the men that were in the power of it.
It is not what God intends, but it is the simple fact.
May the Lord grant grace to each one of us that the number in the power of the present testimony may be increased, for His pleasure and glory, and for His Name’s sake!
